WELCOME TO DTU CHEMICAL ENGINEERING
DTU Chemical Engineering's main activities lie within the areas of product design, process design and production in the chemical, pharmaceutical, food and energy technology industries.
Learn more about our research
Research centers and units
AT CERE, Applied Thermodynamics – Center for Energy Resources Engineering
At the AT CERE Research Centre it is our objective to meet the challenges of today’s petroleum, chemical, material and biotech industries through deep insights, innovative discoveries and the highest level of international research expertise.
BioCon, Biological Conversions group
In the research group Biological Conversions group, BioCon, it is our goal to develop and validate new technologies based on the use of microorganisms as a tool to convert organic waste and wastewater to useful biproducts, biofuel and bioenergy.
PROSYS, Process and System Engineering Center
Our main purpose is to perform research and provide education that will contribute to advancing technologies for future more sustainable (Bio)chemical production processes. Our activities also include digitalization of production processes and we address societal challenges, contributing to the Sustainable Development Goals.
CHEC, Catalysis and High-temperature Engineering Centre
At the CHEC Research Centre we focus on chemical engineering principles applied in combustion, harmful emission control, gasification, catalysis, continuous production of pharmaceuticals and advanced measuring technology. Our primary expertise covers chemical reaction engineering and transport phenomena.
CoaST, The Hempel Foundation Coatings Science and Technology Centre
The centre covers coating technologies along the entire value chain from raw materials, over formulation, test and characterization to production and application. In the broad perspective, the centre supports development, production and use of coatings with improved sustainability profiles over the lifetime of the coating.
Danish Polymer Centre - DPC
At the Danish Polymer Centre we play an internationally leading role in the research of extensional rheology, silicone elastomers and synthesis of polymers. Our primary objective is to develop, implement and apply polymers in commercial products to assist and provide support for the Danish as well as international polymer industry.
KT Consortium
KT Consortium is an industry-academia collaboration where members are provided networking opportunities and state-of-the-art methods and tools for chemical and biochemical engineering with emphasis in Process Systems Engineering (PSE), applied thermodynamics and property prediction.
PILOT PLANT, Centre for Experimental Process and Equipment Design
At PILOT PLANT our main activities are based on the path from laboratory scale to pilot scale experimental processes with a strong focus on industrial practice.
Cooperation
Interested in a research cooperation?
We cooperate with Danish industry, research-based international companies and acknowledged universities around the globe all working within chemistry, biotech, pharma, foods and energy.
Contact us if you would like to know more about cooperation opportunities.

The Fermentation Based Biomanufacturing Initiative
The Fermentation Based Biomanufacturing Initiative provides research-based expert education in fermentation on Master-, PhD-, and professional level.
Accelerated Innovation in Manufacturing Biologics (AIM-Bio)
An international collaborative addressing the future needs of the biopharmaceutical industry.
Thinking about doing a PhD?
Thinking about doing a PhD? Curious about what our PhD students do research about? Learn more about our PhD programme, and watch PhD students explain their research through videos made by themselves.
Summer University
Every year we invite students from all over the world to join a specially designed, experimental course in chemical engineering and process technology. The course takes place in our large and modern pilot plant facilities.
Annual Reports and Graduate School Yearbooks
Each year we publish an annual report along with a graduate school yearbook to give you an insight into our many research projects, results and activities.

DTU researchers receive grants from the Villum Foundation

Foam to seal deep wounds and prevent amputations
With support from the Innovation Fund, the start-up AleSac is developing a foam-based wound-treatment product designed to improve the treatment of deep, complex wounds.
